inputs.original_text: More than 58 lakh people have had their names deleted from West Bengal’s electoral rolls, while the promised tribunals to challenge those removals remain unready despite the Supreme Court’s direction. The software exists; the basic question of where hearings will happen is still being discussed. That is not a harmless procedural snag. When people’s right to vote depends on navigating a system that has not even been put in place, the burden falls hardest on those with the least time, money, and access to bureaucratic power. A right without a timely, meaningful appeal is a right the state is failing to protect.
inputs.modified_text: A clean electoral roll is essential to public confidence, but removing more than 58 lakh names while the promised challenge tribunals remain unready is an administrative failure that cannot be brushed aside. The Supreme Court’s direction should be carried out, not left hanging while officials still debate where hearings will take place. People must be able to challenge errors promptly and fairly; otherwise the state weakens trust in the very process that gives elections their legitimacy. The answer is not to abandon scrutiny, but to make the system work—swiftly, lawfully, and with respect for every eligible voter.
